scope: ephemeral two-host HTTPS writer-generation revocation and witness-DB rollback probe; not independent validation

counterexample.statement: After required writer generation 2 revoked the generation-1 writer and a generation-2 replacement advanced successfully, restoring the pre-revocation witness SQLite snapshot removed the revocation record and the generation-1 writer could advance sequence 2 again.
counterexample.boundary: This is a direct witness-database rollback on the same operator-controlled host. It demonstrates that writer-generation revocation is not rollback-resistant without a separately protected monotonic generation anchor or durable anti-rollback storage.

setup_notes: Port 4445 had no listener before the probe.
The first post-restore one-line SQLite inspection failed from PowerShell/Python quoting after the database restore had already completed; state was rechecked with a short local script.

The first server restart after restored-state inspection failed because the helper was named inspect.py and shadowed Python's standard-library inspect module; the helper was deleted and the same restored DB was restarted without modification.
A __pycache__ directory remained after script cleanup and was removed before final cleanup verification.
limitations: Both computers remain under the same operator and are not independent custody or independent validation.
Writer-generation administration is an in-process/off-path store operation in this research increment.
The revocation generation is stored in the witness SQLite database and can be rolled back with the database.
Credential issuance, rotation, revocation authority, hardware binding and external identity governance are not established.
Witness-host compromise, durable anti-rollback storage and availability loss remain outside the demonstrated protection.
This probe does not establish live containment, matched efficacy, comparator parity, scientific N, canonical efficacy or high assurance.
